Welcome to the gesture data gathering screen!

This is part of an NLnet-funded project striving to produce a fully open source gesture typing library capable of replacing the closed source Google library.
The result is planned to be a simple replacement for AOSP-based keyboards, but also usable with other keyboards, e.g. FlorisBoard.

For developing the library, it is tremendously helpful to have detailed gesture data in different languages and by different users available.
By gathering and submitting gesture typing data you can contribute to an open set of gesture data that will used for library development. The dataset will be published under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license some time after the data gathering phase is finished on %s. Once you have collected data, you can submit it using the share icon on the bottom of this screen.

The \"safe\" way to contribute there is the active gathering mode, where you are shown a specific word, and enter this word using gesture typing.
You can also use the background gathering mode, where you can provide samples from your normal gesture typing from other apps. Due to the sensitivity of this approach, this is opt-in, configurable, and has a review screen for the data you\'re about to submit.

Privacy

 The data you submit consists of target word, keyboard layout and dimensions, gesture (times and coordinates), suggestions by the current library, hash of the used dictionaries, app version, data gathering mode, whether the gesture typing library is the "default" Google library, and an ID to go with each gesture.
 Submitted data will be downloaded and deleted from the ProtonMail mailbox where it is stored at our earliest convenience. After the gesture data gathering phase has ended, the accumulated data set from all users will be published under the Creative Commons BY-SA 4.0 license.


As part of trying to protect your privacy, you won't be listed explicitly as an author. Your credit will be as "The HeliBoard Gesture Data Project Contributors." It should not be possible to connect the data you generate in this screen to your identity. However, it might be possible to determine which gestures were made by the same person. This can be done e.g. from a custom keyboard layout, keyboard dimensions, language, or individual gesturing style.
Note that the email address is intended for data submissions, you may not get fast or consistent replies.
You can share already submitted data again, in case you\'re not sure it was received correctly. We detect and remove duplicates when processing the data.

Data is saved manually via the toolbar key

Turning on background data collection allows AI Keyboard to record gestures you type in other apps. This is very useful for the gesture typing project as it can produce a considerable amount of data, albeit at lower quality than active gathering. Background data collection is not a replacement for actively gathered data, it is meant to be an addition, as data quality is more important than quantity.

 Background gathering has high potential of collecting data that you may consider too private to share, even when published anonymously. For this reason we want to clarify when gesture data is being gathered, and how you can influence it.

 You can find a video explaining more about background data gathering in the links section at the bottom right of this screen.

Any time gesture data may be recorded, you will see an indicator icon in the bottom left of the keyboard. When the circle is filled, at least one gesture has been collected and is waiting to be saved. Data is saved either using the toolbar key (see %1$s) or automatically (when %2$s is disabled). Automatic saving usually happens when switching text fields or closing the keyboard, but may also happen if the text field changes for some other reason. When data is being saved, the indicator will turn green for a short time.
How to control what is saved

Independent of the settings, background data gathering is disabled when using incognito mode. It is also disabled for input fields marked as sensitive (passwords, email, or whenever the input field requests the keyboard to not learn the words). Only words that are in a main dictionary (built-in or from the dictionaries repository) will be collected.

Using %1$s you can select which apps you want to allow background data gathering in. The default setting disables every app, with opt-in per app. You can choose to instead enable every app, and opt-out per app. Doing so is more convenient, but will automatically allow data collection from newly installed apps. This could cause data to be collected which you did not expect.

With %2$s you can exclude specific sensitive words. When gesturing an excluded word, the indicator icon will still show the filled icon (\"data waiting to be saved\"), but the data will be discarded when normally it would be saved. Any blocked words that have already been saved before the word was blocked, will be discarded on exporting data.
Note that background gathering will only collect words that are already in a main dictionary, so the only words you will probably need to block are common words that could be used to personally identify you such as: your name, street, city, territory, etc.

When %3$s is enabled, data is saved only if you choose to do so manually using the %4$s toolbar key (see below). If data is not saved, pending data will be deleted when changing input field or closing the keyboard.
App and word exclusions still apply in this mode.

The %4$s toolbar key can be used to control data gathering. The effect of a press depends on the current state: When background gathering is disabled, it will be enabled.
A long-press will disable gathering for five minutes.
You can re-enable background data gathering earlier with a normal key press.
When %3$s is enabled, pending data will be saved.
Otherwise, pending data will be discarded.

Using %1$s screen you can check and filter the gathered data, delete data you consider too sensitive, and share data. The delete and share buttons will operate on the filtered data, or on the selection if you use long-press to select words. (Note that the \"normal\" share icon outside the %1$s screen will only share data from active gathering.)
The order of shared data is randomized, so nothing more than the individual words can be deduced.
If you want to view the full data that is stored for a gesture, you can share it to a file, and load the file in Swipe-O-Scope.

How the music of the car radio is paused while you dictate. Call on the phone: the call sound stays on the phone (a short dip of 0.2–0.3 s, a quieter recording that the keyboard raises). Call via the car: the call sound goes to the car (the phone is deaf for about a second at the start, a louder recording).
